utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Good morning, Madam Registrar and everybody, all the accused are here. I notice the absence of Mr. Haynes, Mr. Bourgon, that's it. And Prosecution, it's Mr. McCloskey and Mr. Thayer who are present. All right. We can -- Mr. Thayer -- good morning to you, Mr. Lazic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And good day as well. Mr. Thayer, good morning to you. You may proceed and conclude and we'll pick it up from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good morning to you and Your Honours. Good morning, everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Colonel, good morning.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I just have one or two final questions for you. The first concerns a document which we looked at yesterday from the Drina Corps command to the command of the Uzice Corps. Do you remember that document?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't remember that document. I mean, I remember from yesterday what I saw then, but otherwise from before in practice I didn't see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. That's all I was asking about. The Presiding Judge had a question about a document or an order number that was referred to in that document. Do you remember that question from His Honour, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Last night I located that document. If we could just show it on e-court and I just wanted to follow-up and see if you have any recollection about this document. I have a hard copy here if that's easier, but we should have it on e-court momentarily. And that's 3385.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would like to have a hard copy if possible, the paper version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Usher, if you could assist.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I've seen the document now.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. We see that it's a communication from the Uzice Corps command to the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It is now okay. All right. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: We can see from the document, Colonel, that it is dated 25 January 1993. It's from the Uzice Corps command to the Drina Corps command, references various axes that the Uzice Corps has been involved in. And in paragraph 3 refers to establishing cooperation and then paragraph 4 refers to exchanging information. Does this refresh your recollection at all as to cooperation between these two corps during the operations in 1993?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time I was in the Main Staff - and I don't know about this communication along the Drina Corps-Uzice Corps line, I've never seen this document before and I didn't know about this form of communication.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Let me just ask you this: In your experience in the Main Staff and as a corps commander, would this type of communication between a corps in Serbia and a corps in Bosnia and Herzegovina, would that have typically been communicated or made known to the Main Staff of the VRS?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As a rule, this type of communication should have gone through the Main Staff not directly between the two different or several different corps. That's in my opinion. So what they should have done is to inform the Main Staff too. I don't know if the Main Staff was indeed informed or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And, sir, what is your recollection with respect to cooperation between these two corps during the Krivaja 95 operation?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that there was any cooperation during that period of time, during the Drina Corps, that is, and the Uzice Corps. I don't think there was in fact, no cooperation.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, Colonel, during May and June of 1995, how many times do you recall standing in for the Drina Corps commander?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not once. I don't think I did that once on behalf of the Drina Corps commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let's just look at one last document and this is 65 ter 3361, please. Just take a moment and take your time to read the document and acquaint yourself with it, please.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you move it down a bit, please. Could you move it down a bit further, please. More, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: If you're done reading paragraph 3, we'll go to the next page, Colonel.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. If we look at the last lines on the lower left, what does that say there, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says: "Standing in for the commander, Colonel Milenko Lazic."

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And if we could go back to the first page of this document we see that it's dated 8 June of 1995 and it references a Main Staff order 03/4-1165, dated two days prior, the 6th of June. And in the order section it refers to getting together Drina Corps units to form a battalion and various brigades are given tasks further down, including the Zvornik Brigade, if we look at paragraph 2.1.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you recall issuing this order as standing in for the commander of the Drina Corps in June -- early June of 1995, Colonel?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't really remember now precisely, but I have to tell you that standing in for the commander, if somebody's going to do that you need an order and this was probably a temporary absence on behalf of the commander and the order had some sort of urgency, so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: As a matter of principle, I believe that it is fair for the -- toward the witness to show him whole document, not to ask him whether he signed it and he hasn't opportunity to see all document.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, we spent a couple minutes looking at the document. I don't understand the objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's not a long document and it was on the screen. I could see it myself in his language. So let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, if you would, you were saying that -- I'll just quote the beginning portion of your answer, you said: "I can't really remember now precisely, but I have to tell you that standing in for the commander, if somebody's going to do that you need an order and this was probably a temporary absence on behalf of the commander and the order had some sort of urgency ..." My question to you then, sir, is: Was it the case in your experience in the Drina Corps command that if there were a temporary absence of the commander or the Chief of Staff, would you on those occasions be delegated or be temporarily standing in if for just that limited occasion?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, obviously there was no person who was more senior in the command than me, so I was expected to sign it because the document was urgent.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Well, my question to you, sir, is: In your prior answer you suggested that as in the case earlier on in the spring of 1995 when there was a formal appointment that you were to assume the role of standing in for General Krstic because of his extended medical leave, as opposed to that situation where you had a formal order because everybody knew he was going to be unable to carry out his duties for that period of time; as I understand what you're saying, in some limited circumstances, an emergency or where the commander or Chief of Staff for some reason is temporarily absent, on those occasions you did stand in for the commander or the Chief of Staff. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that was the customary practice.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And you didn't need any formal order to do that because it was of such a temporary nature, just to make it clear?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were just solutions for urgent cases, otherwise I didn't have the right to issue orders or anything similar in practice as a general rule.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Colonel, I thank you. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Thayer. Now, Mr. Popovic -- Mr. Zivanovic, redirect?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: How long do you require, how much time?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I have some videos to play, and I believe that it will require --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay, go ahead, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Lazic.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm going to limit my cross-examination to just one portion of the questions put to you by my colleague Mr. Thayer, and they relate to document 3373. So could we have that document put up on e-court, please. It's the order of the 25th of January -- well, it's not an order. It's a document of the 25th of January, 1993, and you explained it to us yesterday and said that something had to be done to protect the civilian population and that this is a document referring to the protection of the civilian population in fact. Now, I'm going to show you a video and I'm just going to ask you - and I'd like to remind you of -- well, take a look at the video and I'll ask you a question after that.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Here we are at the bridge of Skelani and here the street of Bajina Basta, civilians died 16th, 17th, that is the 16th of January ..."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't see anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Well, we have to run it again, please, if you don't mind.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters note that the voice is inaudible and we're reading from the text provided to us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. I appreciate that.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "As far as we heard here in Bajina Basta, civilians were killed on the 16th -- 17th, that is, 16th, 16th of January. "Where is the hospital? "There behind the van. "It started on the 16th at 4.30 in the morning. Suddenly they had distributed their forces throughout the whole range, roughly 16 to 17 kilometres, maybe 700 fighters strong. "On which line was that? "It was on the line all the way up to the hydro-electric power-plant, the lake and the dam, the way up to Crvice. On the way up there we lost many people. They even killed children as people came out of their houses. They killed without any mercy. Then our forces went into action straight away, there was no panic, besides the civilian population who also in the attempt to get away were killed and the results are clearly visible. "Is there any data about how many Serbs died, mainly civilians, and then how many soldiers? "Around 15 soldiers lost their lives, while the rest were civilians. There are still some people listed as missing, not a large number, but around 50 victims in total. "And how many died on their side? "Well, we intercepted them and they lost 150 to 200 men approximately. "So it was a massive attack? "Yes, of course. "Which of the villages there? "The villages are Kusici, Visocnik, Drvnik, Malta, Zarkovici, that part there Kalimanici, a part of that, they stormed into the whole of Kalimanici. Eight of the Ustashas remained. Arapovici, that is where we had most of the victims. Well, it's presumed that around 17 people lost their lives, not only fighters. "Okay. What is your name? "My name is Maksimovic, Vladimir, nickname Buco. "In Bajina Basta Dr. Milos Nincic will explain to us how they were organized when they received the wounded and injured in the massacre in Skelani which happened on that particular day. "Since the whole of the previous year we were under imminent danger of war because of the aggression of the Muslim forces against the territory of the autonomous Republika Srpska and on the territory of our municipality of Skelani, in a way we did enforce certain measures of readiness, duty shifts, so as to be able at any given moment to respond to" --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Sorry, we can stop here, but I intended to show --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, but what's the big idea? At the end of the day I think you can put the question that I am and my colleagues are anticipating anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Lazic, Mr. Lazic, the doctor gave the exact date when the incident took place and that was the 16th of January, 1993, but the year wasn't stated on the video. All it said was the date, January the 16th. Now, what I wanted to ask you is this: Do you perhaps remember this particular incident that took place nine days before your act came into being?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember. The situation was very unpleasant and Bajina Basta was under threat. On the bridge, actually, from Bajina Basta to Skelani some children were even killed. I heard about that. I knew about that in general terms, but I did not know that the Uzice Corps, which is logical, had to intervene. I didn't know that. I didn't know how far the Uzice Corps had to intervene and what it did.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Just tell me this, please. Do you happen to know, when you say that the Uzice Corps had to intervene, can you explain why, why did it have to intervene?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I said that the action going on in the Skelani region flowed over across the Drina River and engulfed the territory of Serbia as well. There was shooting on the territory of Serbia as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm going to show you another brief excerpt from the same video, and it is 8 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Here we are at the bridge in Skelani -- "The artillery and mortars, the wounded on this side -- there weren't any wounded on this side of the Drina River but Radojke Milovanovic, let's hear her story." Could counsel give us a reference, please, for the interpreters to be able to find the section?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic, the interpreters are asking for a reference so that they can follow and translate.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: It is -- it is toward the end of the video. It is sixth paragraph on the third -- on the third page of the video -- on the second page -- on the third page of the -- on the third page they have -- they provided with the text of this video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The problem is they can't find the relevant passage. How does it begin to read?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: "The media objectively stated the jihad warriors were targeting the" --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Thank you, we have found it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: If necessary, we can start from the beginning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Well, I don't know if it is necessary to see the video at all if you have a question which can be answered without --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: It is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: How long this clip?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: 30 seconds, 40 seconds.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Then go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "The media objectively stated the jihad warriors were targeting the Yugoslav side with their artillery, their mortars, but what was reported that there were no wounded on this side of the Drina. Here is Radojke Milovanovic who was wounded in Yugoslavia, so let us hear her story. "There were five to six wounded from my group, Dobrila, whom I know, Dusanka also, Borka and myself, the four of us, I believe. There is more but I haven't seen that. We are from that group that were wounded over here over the bridge. "So you crossed over? "Yes, we did."

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Lazic, does this excerpt confirm that some people were wounded in the territory of Yugoslavia as well on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, obviously.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: What about the Yugoslav authorities or the Army of Yugoslavia, did they have the task to protect their population and territory?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is one of the basic tasks of any armed forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You saw where this took place. Is it near Uzice?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Uzice is a bit further afield, but it is the main town in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether this place, this part, was in the area of defence of the Uzice Corps?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I wanted to ask you this: Are you familiar with any attacks which took place in December, such as an attack against the village of Bjelovac, and I have in mind 1992? Have you ever heard of that?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was when the Muslim forces, or rather, the forces of the Army of B&H launched an attack from the area of Srebrenica. They were very active, destroying the villages in the area of Skelani and Bratunac in particular.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I wanted to play another excerpt.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Unless we have a reference, we cannot read the text and it is completely inaudible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Did you take note of that, Mr. Zivanovic? The interpreters need a reference as before.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: It's the tape number 6, aftermath of attack on Bjelovac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is that okay, interpreters, please?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We found it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Stop here, please, and I will play it from 3.58.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "This is Matic, Snjezana, our lab assistant who died in Bjelovac. She received a wound to the right thigh and she also suffered some suspicious tears on her neck and face and on her left cheek. She is the first to arrive here. Most of these are gun-shot wounds."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Stop, stop, stop. What's your question, Mr. Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: My question, Mr. Lazic, is this: Was the Drina Corps tasked with protecting the Serbian population in the area of Bjelovac and the villages where this crime took place?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course they did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Did you have to show him that video to put this question?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I haven't --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Come on, Mr. Zivanovic --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: -- showed him --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's move. Come on. I mean, please keep in mind that you have four Judges here, four professional Judges, and not a panel of lay jurors.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, but it was the subject of the cross-examination of my learned --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But everyone knows that crimes were committed --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I have to corroborate --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- you don't need to show all this. I mean, playing for the gallery, to the gallery -- what? You could have put the question just the same without showing the video.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I have another similar videos if Trial Chamber didn't like to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What are you -- what are you alleging? Maybe the Prosecution will stipulate?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: For example, that Cerska was attacked as well and same crimes took place in Cerska as well, and I call -- Cerska was the subject of the cross-examination --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer or Mr. McCloskey, if Mr. McCloskey is still here, are you prepared to agree that Cerska was attacked and let's move?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Was attacked by ABH.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, the Prosecution's position has been clear from the beginning of this case, that we concede that crimes were committed by the ABiH. He can put in the whole Naser Oric judgement if he pleases.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Not only that. We have our decision of November 2006, in which --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: In this case I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So put the question. The question is whether the task of the army was to protect the civilians and Serbian property, et cetera, and of course that's perfectly legitimate. But we don't have to go through one film after another.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I'll do it, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Lazic, these attacks - and I wanted to show you some footage of the attack on Cerska and Skelani and some other places as well, but tell me, were those attacks some of the reasons that the order that we saw was put in place?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was the basic reason for it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: In your view, although you didn't participate in it, the attacks on the territory of Yugoslavia, was that the reason for certain measures undertaken by the Uzice Corps at the time?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Nikolic, do you wish to re-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Presiding Judge, we have no additional questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Faveau, I know -- Mr. Petrusic, sorry, I know that you intend to re-examine this witness. Go ahead, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Lazic.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: I will start with 1995. Briefly, I would like you to have a look at 5D227. Could that please be put in e-court. Let us go to the next page so that we can see it briefly and then we can return to the first page. This commander -- sorry, this document, Mr. Lazic, was signed by Commander Colonel Avdo Palic. Do you know who it is?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I recall, he was the commander of the Zepa Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Please go to page 1 again. As you can see, this document was issued by the Zepa Brigade, that is the 285th Eastern Bosnian Light Brigade Zepa sent to the command of the 2nd Corps and to the command of the 28th Division. I believe you will agree that the Zepa Brigade was a part of the 28th Division?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you wait until the Judges have English translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We don't have the translation of this document in front of us actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Mr. Lazic, this is a combat report which says that pursuant to an order of the person standing in for the commander of the 28th Division from Srebrenica, Major Rasim Becirovic dated the 20th of June, 1995, measures are being undertaken to conduct sabotage activities with a goal of inflicting losses upon the aggressor and as regards its personnel and equipment and to try and divert the amassing of Chetnik forces around Sarajevo. Did you know that in that period of June and around the 20th of June there were such activities on the part of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember there were such activities at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Please scroll down the pages. Thank you. That would suffice. You can see in this document that Colonel Palic is reporting to his command that nine sabotage groups were formed or scouting groups or reconnaissance groups as they termed them. It says the first group is along the area of the highway Zljebovi, Pecnik. The second group is in the area of Rijeka. The third is in the area of Velika-Zepa. The fourth in the area of Solila. The fifth in Crna Rijeka. By the way, I wanted to ask you whether the Crna Rijeka area is also where the command of the Main Staff of Republika Srpska was?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The Main Staff was deployed in Crna Rijeka.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: The sixth group was in the area of Banja Lucica, the seventh again in the area of Crna Rijeka but closer to Bojcino Brdo. The eighth in the area of Karaula, and the ninth in the area of the village of Visnjica. My question is this: All of the sabotage groups that had been formed, were they sent to the territory that was outside the protected areas of Srebrenica and Zepa and under the control of the Army of Republika Srpska or the VRS, that is?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether exactly all of them were sent, but I know something concerning the Visnjica group. They were active and inflicted serious losses among the civilians. The group Crna Rijeka was also active and put the Main Staff itself in danger. There were more frequent attacks towards Krivaca and Solila as well as towards Velika Zepa where our communications centre was. As for the other groups, I'm not familiar with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Please go further down the document. That is enough. The last paragraph says that some 40 Chetniks were killed, dozens were wounded, and a large amount of infantry weapons was seized, among others we see automatic rifles being mentioned, then the machine-guns, radio devices, rounds of ammunition, and other equipment. Are you familiar with the losses referred to by Colonel Palic here?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with any details, but I did hear of some losses.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please could we see document 5D1100 next in e-court -- I apologise, this document has not been translated but it is due to arrive in the system shortly.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Item 3. On that day, the 26th of June, the deputy commander, Major-General Radislav Krstic, reported that the enemy intensified sabotage group incursions in particular from the enclaves of Zepa and Srebrenica. Were you familiar with that on the 26th?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Please go back up to the very beginning of the document. In the second paragraph it states that in the area of the Milici Brigade an enemy sabotage group 15 to 20 soldiers strong from Zepa at 4.30 routed our forward detachment at the Klicac feature and entered the village of Visnjica. Further in the report it is stated that one soldier was killed, a sergeant was wounded as well as one woman, five houses were set on fire, and the cattle driven away. On the 26th -- well, is that the attack on Visnjica that you refer to?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: And of course would you agree with me that the command of the Drina Corps was fully informed about it all?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we go back to page 2 of the document now, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Tell us who signed this document, please.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Major-General Radislav Krstic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Is that his signature or ...

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think it's his signature because you have the word "za," meaning "for," so somebody signed for him.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Is this your signature?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, it isn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Now let's have document 107, please -- P107 the number is. And let's go straight to page 2 if we may. Mr. Lazic, I think you're familiar with this document. It is an order for active combat operation issued by the command of the Drina Corps, Milenko Zivanovic. Can we go down the document to see point 2. Mr. Lazic, in paragraph 2 we've already commented on it, the Drina Corps command pursuant to directives 7 and 7/1 of the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska and on the basis of the situation in the area of responsibility of the corps. Now, my question to you is this and that's the point I'd like to refer to: What do you understand by this? When it says this situation in the area of the corps' responsibility, can that mean the situation, a prior situation, that is to say from the end of June, in which an attack took place by the Muslim sabotage groups on the territory of the Army of Republika Srpska and the burning of this village, Visnjica?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: In your opinion, could that have been a basis for the Drina Corps commander to issue the order for combat action or the start of the attack --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I've let a lot of leading go by, and this is also really when a question is prefaced with "in your opinion," you know. We've had a lot of thoughts and so forthcoming from Colonel Lazic, but if there's any way to base it in any experience to save the question otherwise, it's really sounding like it's eliciting some kind of expert opinion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I won't comment on that. Mr. Petrusic, I'm sure you will continue with your re-examination along the established rules of procedure and avoiding direct or leading questions and not eliciting expert opinion from the witness. Otherwise, please go ahead and try to bring your re-examination to an end as quickly as you can.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Mr. Lazic, is there a connection between the previous attacks and this particular situation, or rather, this order?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: May we now have document 3359 and 3358 put up on e-court, please, if that is technically possible. Mr. Gavric -- I mean Mr. Lazic, on the right-hand side of our screens we have a document issued by Captain Gavric --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, for the witness is it possible to have ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The document has been taken off the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's back again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: If it moves things along, I've got hard copies of both documents I can just give to the witness to look at instead of proceeding this way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think we've got it right now. Thank you. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gavric -- I mean Lazic, the document on the right-hand side of the screen is signed, as you see, by Mico Gavric. Now, was he subordinate, a subordinate officer, to Vidoje Blagojevic, the commander of the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: On the left-hand side you see a report by Commander Blagojevic in which he states that four projectiles were fired.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Now, in Gavric's document it says that this firing took place at 1907 hours. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: And do you see in the document that after this first firing took place that something went wrong with that artillery piece?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Do you happen to know on the basis of what -- how it -- how it happened that Colonel Blagojevic says that four projectiles were fired, whereas Gavric speaks of just one?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I don't know how Captain Gavric could have been writing to the Drina Corps in the first place because he was a subordinate officer, he was subordinate to the Bratunac Brigade. Secondly, Colonel Blagojevic most probably maintained communication with Captain Gavric, so it was on the basis of their conversations that he arrived at that piece of information. That's my opinion.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you whether in Gavric's report there are grounds for Vidoje Blagojevic to say that four projectiles were fired?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Obviously not.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: May we have the next document 4D135, please. This is a report from the Ministry of Defence, the secretariat of defence in Tuzla, the department for Srebrenica municipality, and on the document we have a list of all the business premises used by the armed forces of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Can we pan down, please. Thank you. And at the end of that page under number 4 -- rather, IV it says: "The 282nd East Bosnian Light Brigade in Srebrenica." And then under number I it says: "Uses Hotel Domavija Srebrenica," and the user is the 282nd East Bosnian Light Brigade. In English that should be on page 2. Mr. Lazic, is that a military facility?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is a civilian facility which is used during wartime for military purposes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: From the aspects of the army can it represent a military target?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: In his report and a number, or rather, Exhibit P3359, Colonel Blagojevic states that one shell fell on, or rather, two projectiles fell near the Domavija facility. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: During yesterday's examination-in-chief -- or rather, the examination by the Prosecutor, you said something about how orders were conveyed and passed on. Now, I'm going to show you a document and it is 5D1077. And this is the last document, unfortunately, for which we do not have a translation that we're going to use today. This is a Drina Corps document dated the 25th of May, 1995. May we pan down. Thank you. And it is signed by Major-General Milenko Zivanovic. Mr. Lazic, would you read point 4, please.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Ensure that all anti-aircraft devices be placed on high combat-readiness and monitor the situation constantly in the air-space." I can't see what it says next. Anyway, it says: "Open fire on UNPROFOR planes pursuant to permission given by the Main Staff and open fire without waiting for permission on enemy forces -- enemy forces firing on our forces and civilian targets."

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: So is the corps commander conveying an order from the Main Staff, or rather, General Mladic, saying how to fire, how to open fire?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: And is it General Zivanovic who is conveying this information?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: In the previous case would it only be he, General Zivanovic, or someone of equal standing be in a position to convey orders?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: P3029 is the next document I'd like to have up on e-court now, please. This is a Drina Corps document issued by the Drina Corps on the 24th of November, 1992, signed by Commander Colonel Milenko Zivanovic. Do you remember that the Prosecutor yesterday linked this document up to the directive number 4, directive number 4, and that can be concluded on the basis of his -- of the first paragraph where it says: "Pursuant to the directive strictly confidential number 02/5 of the 19th of November, 1992, the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska," and so on and so forth. So do you remember this document, it was shown to you yesterday?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: May we go to the bottom of the page. Thank you. Can you see the title there, the heading, where it says the object of the operation?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: So underneath that heading what it says is this: "Rout and throw out enemy forces from the area of responsibility of the corps." Then it says the next goal which is the following: "Open up the corridors: Visegrad-Rogatica-Pale and Visegrad-Gorazde-Foca." The next goal: "Rout and throw out of the area of responsibility all paramilitary formations." Then the next goal is to: "Create favourable conditions for the functioning of civilian authority in the liberated towns and throughout the territory in the area of responsibility of the corps." Then it goes on to say: "To create the best possible conditions for members of the Army of Republika Srpska and the population especially during winter in the area of responsibility of the corps." Now, these goals set out in this way, is there anything there which relates to expelling the civilian population from this territory?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There isn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Can we turn to the next page, please. Can we scroll down a bit, please. That's fine. Let us look at point 2 where it says: "Tasks for the units." The first task given to the Zvornik Brigade reads: "In the present area of responsibility conduct or carry out the necessary regrouping and ensure for the main sources the corridor of Zvornik-Crni Vrh-Ceparde and directly link up and ensure coordinated action with elements of the East Bosnian Corps in the area of the eastern slopes of Majevica as well as with elements of the Birac Brigade in the Pandurica-Ceparde area. At the same time, out of the areas of the village of Kostijerevo, Milosevici, Mladjevac, Snagovo, engage in active combat in coordinated action with elements of the Birac and Bratunac Brigades and liberate the general area of the village of Kamenica and have elements of the forces at the ready in the direction of Kalesija." In the task given to the Zvornik Brigade, is there any mention of the expulsion of the civilian population out of the area of Zvornik and the area covered by the Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there isn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Under point 2.2, a task was given to the Bratunac Brigade which I'd like you to read, or rather, I should read it out to you.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: "The Bratunac Brigade has received the task from its command to engage its main forces in order to rout the enemy forces and reach the features of Loznik, Zanik, Caus, and Bijela Stijena, and to engage its other forces in coordinated action with elements of the Birac Brigade to cut off the Srebrenica-Cerska road. Next, to engage in coordinated action with the Birac and Zvornik Brigades in order to liberate the areas of Pobudje, Hrnjice and Konjevic Polje, thus creating all the pre-conditions for the opening the Vlasenica-Milici-Drinjaca road." Next, it says: "The Fakovici Battalion should be consolidated as soon as possible and tasked with reaching as deep within the area of Srebrenica as possible, especially by drawing upon the territories of the Serbian villages and to act towards Srebrenica." Mr. Lazic, in this part of the task I read out to you, is there any mention of the fact that this task given to the Bratunac Brigade has as its goal the expulsion of the civilian population or is there anything that would hint at that?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Obviously it is not directed at Srebrenica as the town proper is concerned. What it does speak of is to -- is the use of the Serb villages -- rather, what is meant by that is that the intention should be to link up the various Serb villages in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: P2742 was also shown to you yesterday. Can we have the document now as well. The document is dated the 1st of May, 1993, from the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska. It was issued by the deputy commander, Major-General Manojlo Milovanovic [phoen]. The document was uploaded into e-court.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters note that they don't have the official translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Do you know that several days after the 1st of May, namely on the 8th of May, Zepa was declared a safe zone, an enclave?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Do you know that an agreement was signed on the cessation of hostilities on both sides?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Do you know if the agreement in question was observed by the Army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Can we now call up -- [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Mr. Petrusic, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] P114 and another document --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Which the interpreter didn't hear because the microphone was off.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- can we place them next to one another. P107 and P114.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Colonel, the document on the right-hand side was issued by the Drina Corps command. It is entitled: "Order for attack on the Zepa enclave." It was issued on the 13th of July, 1995. Did you have occasion to see this document?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not have occasion to see this document because it was issued at the Krivaca forward command post where I was not present and I did not have otherwise the opportunity of seeing it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: This document for the attack on Srebrenica is entitled: "Command for active combat activity." Did both documents originate from the same command?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Do both of the documents relate to enclaves?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us why the 2nd of July document, in the drafting of which you kind of participated, is entitled: "Command for active combat activity," whereas the 13th of July, 1995, document is entitled: "Command for the attack on the Zepa enclave"?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could not account for that. There are no material differences there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Does the character of the combat activities involved, to put it in layman's terms, the character of the combat activities to be carried out, is that something that was in this instance decided upon by the corps commander?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Just to clarify for the record, Mr. President, since we're talking about two different documents, one having to do with Srebrenica, the other one having to do with Zepa, if we could just clarify which the last answer was referring to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Lazic, if you could clarify that for us, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The first document was made at the corps command as a result of the preparations for the conduct of active combat activities in the direction of Srebrenica. This document did not include an attack on Srebrenica, rather, combat activities in the general area, the separation of enclaves -- or rather, it did not imply an attack on Zepa. When the conditions were met on the 13th, as the second document testifies, a subsequent order was issued for an attack on the Zepa enclave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Is that clear enough to you?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: It is. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's proceed, Mr. Petrusic, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Now that we have touched upon this topic, what do -- which activities do combat activities include?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All sort of combat activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry my question had to do with active combat activities.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Active combat activities is a broader term which includes both offensive and defensive combat activity.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Can we now have document P5, the last page of that document. This is directive number 7 issued by the Commander-in-Chief, Dr. Karadzic. [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Mr. Petrusic, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That should be the penultimate page. I'm sorry. Page 21 of the Serbian version. Can we look at the bottom of the page, that's page 15 in fact in e-court in English?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Mr. Lazic, can you please look at point 8 which says: "Send corps commander's decisions for approval to the commander of the VRS Main Staff seven days before carrying out the planned operation." This is my question for you. If the operation Srebrenica was planned on the basis of the directive, did the commander of the Drina Corps have the obligation to send to the commander of the Main Staff the order that he issued for his approval?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the practice applied under normal living and working conditions; however, you will admit that the fact that President Karadzic, as the supreme commander, issued an order was something that was out of the ordinary. And as a result of that, this order was placed in a bit of an awkward situation as testified by this point 8.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Do you wish to say that the commander did not send his order for approval?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he definitely did but he was not able to do it seven days ahead of the planned operation, rather, he was able to do it only when the order was ready, when it was completed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: At any rate, there would have been some sort of written record of it -- or rather, would there have been a written record of it somewhere?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There should have been.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Do you know - and we're not calling for speculation here - that this was, in fact, done?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, any time soon we need to have a break, Mr. Petrusic. How far away are you from finishing your re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, if we take the break now I could have a look at my notes and it is possible that I will have one or two questions or that I will have none. If that is not a problem for you or the witness, I would like us to take the break now, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Not at all, Mr. Petrusic. We'll have a break, as you suggest, 25 minutes and we'll take it up from there. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Petrusic, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Mr. Lazic, for the last time during your testimony we'll go back to P5 which is to your right. You can have a look. Please go to page 8 for you. In e-court it is page 10 in the B/C/S -- sorry, 15, and in the B/C/S version 10. Yes. The Drina Corps, under that heading the task was to completely physically separate the enclaves of Zepa and Srebrenica in order to prevent any communication between the enclaves. On this page, page 8, please read for yourself what operations are being mentioned which were part of the Drina Corps tasks, at least according to this directive. In order to navigate you through the text, I just wanted to tell you that they are all in quotation marks.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what operations are those.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The operation that has to do with the separation of Srebrenica and Zepa, then the Operation Jadar, the Operation Zvijezda, the Operation Spreca.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: What about Operation Zvijezda, does its name also include 95, is its full name Operation Zvijezda 95?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that it was supposed to be carried out in 1995?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was just the name. It needn't necessarily mean that it was supposed to take place in 1995. It probably was planned for that year, but it didn't have to mean necessarily that it would be implemented that year.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: What about Spreca operation, is it also Spreca 95 operation?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Does the same explanation apply to this operation as well?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Do you know why in this task given to the Drina Corps to separate Srebrenica and Zepa no name is mentioned, there is no operation name?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Perhaps it was because the combat activities concerning the separation did not present an operation in itself in the full sense of the words. Those were combat activities that had to do with the separation of the two enclaves.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Please go to the next page. For you it is page 9. In the English it should be page 11. In any case, the name of the chapter is Herzegovina Corps, therefore, could we please go further down the document. Mr. Lazic -- it is page 12 in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Do you see the penultimate paragraph under the Herzegovina Corps task? It reads: "Until the end of March -- by the end of March 1995 the Herzegovina Corps command shall plan operations for reaching the Neretva river valley named Krivaja 95." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Does this task given to the Herzegovina Corps, Krivaja 95, have anything to do with the Drina Corps task?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It has nothing to do with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: This concludes my examination concerning this document. I have another document which is an intercept, the P number is 1242. Could we please have that brought up on our screens. In the transcript the number should be 1242B. Mr. Lazic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I just ask for a moment, if we could, because we're having trouble getting the English transcript up here. I don't know if --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's on e-court --

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Yeah, we're -- that's what we're trying to do. It's just slow on our side for some reason. I just ask for a second so we can see it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, by all means.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: When you're ready, tell me so that we can proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note, we don't have the benefit of the official translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: We have it now, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's move, there's nothing special here. It's a short intercept that we're talking about. Mr. Petrusic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Mr. Lazic, you said that in the period after the planned operation, among others locations, you visited the location where Colonel Vlacic was, that is the Bircani Brigade. I will read out a part of that conversation. The conversation took place between the then-General Krstic by some the corps commander -- or rather, by the presidential decree he was appointed the Drina Corps commander. The date is the 18th of July, time 5.16 p.m. Somewhere around the middle of the first page we have General Krstic who is at the IKM in Krivaca --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, Mr. Petrusic. I hate to interrupt you but you just said 5.16 p.m. In the English translation that we have at the top of the page we have 0716 hours. The document that we see on e-court does mention in the bottom -- does have a reference to Lazic and to Vlacic, but I want to make sure that we're talking of the same -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I think the intercept my friend wishes to show is actually 1142, not 1242, which is what we have on the screen right now. I think if we go there it might be the correct one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, could you check that, Mr. Petrusic, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the intercept I have on my e-court monitor. It is at frequency 255850, time 7 hours 16 minutes. I misspoke.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Then that's fine. That's correct. We have the same one. Thank you. Let's proceed then.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But the number is the correct one.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: General Krstic says to Cerovic -- well, first of all, Mr. Lazic, do you know who Cerovic is?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do, Colonel Cerovic was one of the assistants -- assistant commanders.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Of course he was with the Drina Corps command?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was assistant to the Drina Corps commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Thank you. General Krstic says: "Listen well, Cerovic." Then Cerovic says: "Go ahead. "Krstic: Go down there and command that part. "Cerovic: I understand. "Krstic: Go ahead. "Cerovic: Just listen. Yesterday evening Lazic called in. He said that since Vlacic had arrived he intended to come here. "Krstic: Well, fine, you are the main man there. Is it clear? "Cerovic: Yes, sir. "Krstic: Therefore, convey it to him that you are the main person. "Cerovic: Yes, sir, General. "Krstic: And command in such a way" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, we need to see the second page of this document in English. Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: I want to go on reading. Krstic says: "Command that way. Cerovic says: "Clear." Krstic says: "Pay particular attention to the part to the west of you." The rest of the conversation is not important for us now. Mr. Lazic, did the corps commander have the right to appoint someone to replace him in this or similar situations?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was his right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Did he appoint Cerovic to be his assistant instead of you as the chief of administration?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're wrong. I wasn't administration chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Sorry, Chief of Staff.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't that either.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: What was your position at the time?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Head of the department for training and education -- and operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Does General Krstic appoint Cerovic as the person who was supposed to stand in for him in this conversation?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think this conversation took place after the 13th of July once Krstic had become the corps commander. Cerovic was his assistant. It is most likely that for that reason Krstic decided that he should command from the command post in Vlasenica with the rest of the corps or over the rest of the corps while he was away. I was, therefore, being excluded from any command responsibilities or roles.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Mr. Lazic, I beg your pardon, I forgot what your position was at the time. This was also my last question. I have no further questions of you, and thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Petrusic. That brings to an end the testimony -- your testimony, Mr. Lazic, unless -- yes, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have two questions that arise directly from the re-direct which will take no more than five --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Which re-direct?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: My learned friend from the Miletic team.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's see what the questions are first before we authorise the witness to answer them.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: The first question has to do with a particular document, a 1993 Drina Corps order which my friend spent some time going through in terms of the individual tasks being issued to the brigades and asked very specific questions about whether those specific tasks involved moving out, forcibly removing, the Muslim population. I want to point out one portion of that document which was not shown to the witness during that re-direct examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That -- doesn't a document once it is in the record speak for itself?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: It does, Your Honour, and we can certainly make that a matter of submissions later on. I just, while we were on it, wanted to follow up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The other question?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: The second question has to do with the specific question regarding whether or not there is a written record of the Krivaja 95 plan going to the Main Staff. It was one of the -- I believe the last question my friend asked before the break whether there was -- whether he was aware of any written record of that being done. I wanted to show the witness one document which, in the Prosecution's submission, shows that was the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Just put your second question and forget the first one.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Certainly, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Good morning again, Colonel. You were shown 65 ter 107, which is the Krivaja 95 combat plan. I have a hard copy here for you or we can put it up in e-court. I just ask if we could go to the last page of the English which is page 6 of the B/C/S. And again, this is the 2 July Krivaja 95 combat plan which my friend asked you about and I believe you suggested that it -- you testified that this should have gone to the Main Staff. Let me know when you see that last page.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is correct, that it should have been sent. You can see from the contents, that is to say that one copy should be sent to the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska, that that was compulsive.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Colonel. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Josse.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: It's been done now, but could I ask what the point of that was. It was exactly the same as Your Honours had just ruled in relation to the other document. The document speaks for itself. The evidence is in. Purely gratuitous.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah, you are right, but we couldn't anticipate everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: I'm not blaming the Court, with respect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But you are right. Mr. Lazic, I have checked, verified, with my colleagues whether there are any questions from the Bench, there aren't, which means your testimony ends here. On behalf of the Trial Chamber I would like to thank you for your patience and for having come over to give testimony and on behalf of everyone we wish you a safe journey back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Now, exhibits. Has the full list been circulated?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Popovic Defence team, Mr. Zivanovic or --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I sent the list of my --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, you have just two documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, this is videos.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Two of them are shown to the witness, two of them are not shown according to your --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But you are still introducing them?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: None, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: From the other Defence teams? None. So these are so admitted, and they will be given the correct reference number later on. Miletic Defence team, there is a whole list here going into a page and little bit on the second. You confirm that, Madam Faveau and Mr. Petrusic?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: No, Mr. President. We just ask that for those documents for which there are no English translations, that they be marked for identification, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Marked for identification, and that's how it will be. The rest are admitted -- admitted. Okay. Mr. Nikolic, I don't recall you making use of documents, but do you have any documents that you wish to tender?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Prosecution exhibits, we have a list that has been circulated. Any objections on the part of the Defence teams? Yes, Ms. Faveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Document 3376, it is the witness statement of Milenko Lazic. The Prosecutor read the relevant part of this statement and it is now on the transcript, but this statement has not been shown to the witness and we did not see the B/C/S version of it. So I don't really know whether the witness has really signed and read the statement -- whether he has checked this statement or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Madam. Yes, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, this is an error. That document is -- shouldn't be on our list. We never received a B/C/S version of it, but I did read the portion in so there's no need to introduce the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, but that portion is in the record. I previously saw you, Mr. Josse.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: I was going to make that exact submission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. All these documents minus 3376 are admitted. Thank you. And that concludes the testimony of Mr. Lazic. Next witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And welcome to this Tribunal. You're about to start giving evidence. Our Rules require that before you do so you make a solemn declaration that you will be testifying the truth. Madam Usher is handing you now the text of the solemn declaration. Please read it out aloud and that will be your solemn undertaking with us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Please make yourself comfortable.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Tapuskovic, who is appearing for accused Popovic in this case, will now be asking you some questions. She will then be followed on cross-examination by some, one or more, of the Defence teams, other Defence teams, and then by the Prosecution. Madam Tapuskovic, and if you could please introduce yourself for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everybody else in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, the Trial Chamber has already introduced me to you, but let me repeat for the record. My name is Mira Tapuskovic and I am the Defence team of Mr. Vujadin Popovic. Sir, I'd like to ask you to answer questions that I'm going to put to you here and now. I'm going to ask them slowly so that you can follow the transcript on the screen. And since you and I speak the same language, to avoid overlapping which will create a problem in the courtroom, both for the interpreters but especially for the exactitude of recording what was said, I would like to ask you to follow the screen and to see how the text appears on the screen so that you can answer properly and slowly. Thank you. Could you tell us for the record your name and surname first, please.

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: My name is Pero Mijatovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us where and when you were born.

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: I was born on the 23rd of October, 1955, in Sokolac.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you now in two or three sentences briefly tell us what education you have had.

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: I'm a graduate from the faculty of economics of the university in Sarajevo. I graduated in 1978. I was a regular student enrolled at that university.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When you graduated from the faculty of economics, where did you gain employment first? Give us a brief description of how you progressed professionally.

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: After graduation I started working straight away in commercial firms, and later on I got a job in the insurance fund in Sarajevo. And I stayed in that institution until 1992, and when I moved to Sarajevo to work in the agency -- in the housing agency of that same insurance fund.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You said that you moved there in 1992 because your job took you there. Can you tell us now what you did during the war in the territory of the former Yugoslavia from 1992 to 1992 [as interpreted], professionally speaking where did your job take you?

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: I left Sarajevo at the beginning of 1992, left my job there, and I went to Sokolac once again. After that, when the order for mobilisation was issued, I became activated and became a member of the 1st Romanija Infantry Brigade, the 3rd Company of the 1st Battalion, in fact, as an ordinary private, a soldier.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me this now, please. Up until what time were you in the Army of Republika Srpska, what period?

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: On the 1st of November, 1993, pursuant to an agreement reached between two ministries and pursuant to the request of the Ministry of the Interior, the need was seen for replenishment of an inspector in commercial crime in the public security centre of Sarajevo Birac centre. They asked for ten inspectors, there was an opening for ten inspectors, economics graduates and army members, who would put their names down in the competition for a job in the crime prevention centre in Osijek --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Department of crime prevention, interpreter's correction. Not Osijek but crime prevention department.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So I put my name forward, I passed all the tests, and I was accepted as an employee of the centre on the 1st of November, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. How long did you stay working in the service of the Ministry of the Interior, up until what year?

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: I worked as an inspector for commercial crime in Osijek for crime prevention --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Once again interpreter's correction: Crime prevention department.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I then worked in Serbian Sarajevo until the 30th of June, 2004.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have to intervene. Page 45, line 19 and page 46, line 3, it says "Osijek," which is a place in Croatia; and what the witness said, he said "department" or "section." So not Osijek but "odsjek," meaning department or sector, section.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you for that, Madam Tapuskovic. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell us, Mr. Mijatovic, whether at some period during your employment within the frameworks of the Ministry of the Interior were engaged by this Tribunal; and if so, describe what you did briefly.

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: Pursuant to instructions from the Tribunal sent to the crime police administration in Banja Luka in 2001 or maybe 2002, I'm not quite sure now because it's just a few months' difference, anyway a telegram was sent, a dispatch was sent, requesting an experienced inspector employed in the sector to be attached and take part in financial investigations which were requested by the Tribunal. I received instructions from the administration of the crime prevention police to place myself at the disposal of the investigators, to take part in assisting them in financial -- conducting financial investigations.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: This lasted with several interruptions over a period of several months.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, this kind of work, work on assignments like that, did it require special permission or certificates of any kind, if I can put it that way?

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: The job did require, not only for me personally but for all members of the MUP, a state examination which had to be passed and there were other checks and training courses, lectures, and tests and examinations, physical ones, it required a knowledge of the law and regulations, and all legal regulations. And once that process had been completed, of education and training and once we had been tested, a certificate was issued allowing us to work in the area of white collar crime or commercial crime.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the witness mentioned a certificate of the IPTF which was not recorded, so I'd like to ask him the following.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mijatovic, IPTF, is that the International Police Test Force from Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Task force, interpreter notes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
